channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency Investigates Allegations of Fraudulent Property Purchases
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency (FMA) has investigated claims that a relative of Perizat Kairat purchased apartments in Dubai with money obtained through fraud. The agency stated that the allegation, which spread via an anonymous Telegram channel, was not confirmed. The FMA previously noted Kairat's misuse of charitable funds for personal purchases.

item.title: Yandex Addresses Erroneous Money Deductions for Kazakhstan Users Following Service Disruptions
item.description: Yandex is investigating and addressing erroneous money deductions experienced by users in Kazakhstan following recent service disruptions. The company stated that while many services are gradually being restored, some payment functions may still encounter errors or delays. Yandex assured users that each case of incorrect charges will be reviewed, though support response times may be longer due to increased demand.

item.title: Afghanistan Reports Progress in Preventing Child Marriage Amid UNICEF's Call for Action
item.description: Afghanistan's Ministry of Vice and Virtue reports preventing several cases of forced and underage marriages in the past five months, including attempts to marry girls aged six and eight. UNICEF urges increased investment in girls' education, healthcare, and protection, highlighting child marriage's detrimental effects and advocating for girls' continued access to education.

item.title: Top Global Crypto Funds Invest Billions in Astana Tech Project
item.description: Kazakhstan-based tech project Network School has secured multi-billion dollar investments at a $2 billion business valuation. Major international venture capital and crypto players, including Polychain Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, and Coinbase, are participating. The announcement was made at the Network State Conference 2026.

item.title: Azerbaijan-Kazakhstan Cooperation Could Reshape Central Asian Integration
item.description: Azerbaijan's participation in the Central Asian heads of state consultative meeting offers a key trade outlet, potentially reorienting regional integration. Closer cooperation between Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan on cross-Caspian transport could strengthen the corridor, making it an axis for industrial projects and trade. This collaboration could provide an alternative route for Central Asian exports, bypassing traditional transit paths.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Nuclear Data Center Project Receives Backing from Japanese Firm
item.description: A Japanese company has agreed to cooperate on a 50-megawatt data center project in Uzbekistan, potentially becoming the world's first powered by a small modular nuclear reactor. This initiative is linked to Uzbekistan's first nuclear power plant, under construction with Russian involvement. The data center project aims to leverage nuclear energy for IT infrastructure.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Agree to Expand Cooperation in Key Sectors
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium will broaden cooperation in critical areas including critical minerals, transport and logistics, artificial intelligence, energy, agriculture, and education. The leaders of both nations adopted a joint statement following talks during a state visit, aiming to develop friendly relations based on equality and mutual benefit.

item.title: Flash Floods Predicted in Tajikistan Over the Next Two Days
item.description: Tajikistan's Hydrometeorological Agency has warned residents of potential flash floods on October 13 and 14. Heavy rainfall is expected to cause floods in mountainous and foothills regions of Sughd, Khatlon, districts of republican subordination, and western Gorno-Badakhshan. Residents are advised to take precautions.

item.title: New Acting Governor Appointed for Sirdaryo Region
item.description: Zaynilobiddin Nizomiddinov has been appointed as the acting governor of Sirdaryo region. He was previously the governor of Bekobod district. A source in the government confirmed his appointment to Daryo.uz. Nizomiddinov has been released from his previous position.

item.title: Man Arrested for Demanding $840,000 for Construction Permits in Bostanliq
item.description: A 56-year-old man has been arrested in Tashkent for allegedly demanding $840,000 to secure permits for constructing residential buildings on 4 hectares of non-residential land in Bostanliq district, Tashkent region. The Interior Ministry reported the man, a construction materials trader, promised to obtain the permits through contacts in the State Cadastre Agency.

item.title: Houthi Rebels Attack Riyadh Airport Three Times, Causing Casualties
item.description: Yemeni Houthi rebels have attacked Riyadh's international airport three times since early October. Attacks on October 10-11 resulted in at least 14 deaths and hundreds injured. The report notes the website is blocked but accessible via a provided link.

item.title: UN Rights Envoy Urges ICC to Probe Alleged Pakistani War Crimes in Afghanistan
item.description: UN special rapporteur Richard Bennett is calling on the International Criminal Court (ICC) to investigate alleged Pakistani war crimes in Afghanistan. He cited civilian casualties from cross-border violence and a deadly airstrike on a Kabul drug rehabilitation hospital, urging accountability.

item.title: King Philippe of Belgium Thanks Kazakhstan for Hospitality During State Visit
item.description: King Philippe of Belgium expressed gratitude to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev for Kazakhstan's hospitality during his state visit. He noted the strong ties established over thirty years and expressed optimism about future cooperation. The King highlighted Belgium's significant investment in Kazakhstan's economy and acknowledged the country's growing international standing and economic growth.

item.title: King of Belgium Speaks Kazakh in Astana, Praises Nation's Heritage and AI Progress
item.description: During a joint briefing with President Tokayev in Astana, King Philippe of Belgium addressed Kazakh citizens with the traditional blessing "Shanyragynyz biik bolsyn!" He praised Kazakhstan's rich heritage, hospitality, and its position as a leader in artificial intelligence development. The King expressed eagerness to explore historical sites and cultural richness.

item.title: Expert: Kazakhstan's Anti-Human Trafficking Reforms Can Serve as Regional Model
item.description: Kazakhstan is enhancing its anti-human trafficking system through legislative reforms, expanded victim support, and international cooperation. Special attention is given to protecting individuals from modern forms of exploitation, including forced involvement in cybercrime. An ANI editor praised the country's reforms, noting their focus on prevention and victim rights restoration.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium Sign Dozens of Bilateral Agreements
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belgium are set to sign numerous bilateral agreements following productive talks between President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and King Philippe. The leaders confirmed their commitment to strengthening a multifaceted partnership, noting the absence of political disagreements. Key areas for expanded cooperation include transport, logistics, critical minerals, energy, industry, agriculture, biotech, digitalization, and space technologies. Business forums and roundtables are expected to finalize these agreements.

item.title: President Discusses Cultural and Humanitarian Agreements with Belgium
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev shared details of cultural and humanitarian agreements reached with Belgium. He confirmed intentions to establish direct ties between universities, museums, and cultural institutions, and to develop joint educational programs. The President expressed gratitude for showcasing Belgian art in Kazakhstan and supported cooperation between the Almaty Museum of Arts and Centre Pompidou. Agreements were also made to ease travel for service passport holders.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Reports Completion of Tajikistan Border Demarcation
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov announced the completion of border demarcation with Tajikistan. While the physical demarcation is finished, Japarov stated that unresolved issues concerning property of residents in border areas remain. He instructed relevant authorities to resolve compensation matters. Tajik authorities have not commented, though a Tajik official previously indicated full border demarcation with Kyrgyzstan was expected by 2027.

item.title: New Facilities Inaugurated and Major Projects Launched in New Tashkent
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the inauguration of new facilities and the commencement of major projects in New Tashkent. The city's development, initiated three years ago, includes projects worth $50 billion for a safe and green urban environment, featuring 2,000 hectares of green zones and 500 hectares of parks.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and King Philippe Hold Press Briefing
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the historic state visit of the King and Queen of Belgium to Kazakhstan marks a new chapter in bilateral relations and strengthens friendship between the two peoples. He expressed gratitude for the King's leadership and commitment to fostering understanding.

item.title: Kazakhstan Initiates AI Training for 75 Military Personnel at Maqsut Narikbayev University
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched a training program for 75 military personnel, including conscripts, to develop software using artificial intelligence (AI) without traditional coding. The course at Maqsut Narikbayev University focuses on 'vibe coding,' enabling users to create digital tools by describing tasks in natural language.

item.title: Afghanistan's Wildlife Faces Extinction Due to Climate Change and Habitat Destruction, Experts Warn
item.description: Environmental experts in Afghanistan warn that climate change, including rising temperatures and droughts, is threatening wildlife survival by limiting access to water and food. Habitat destruction, illegal hunting, and deforestation exacerbate these threats. Researchers stress the need for accurate statistics, habitat protection, and stricter enforcement of environmental laws to prevent biodiversity loss.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Water Resources Responds to Reports of Amu Darya Drying Up
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Water Resources addressed social media reports claiming the Amu Darya River is drying up. Data from the Termiz hydropost shows water levels are 27 cm higher than last year. While flow at the Kerki hydropost is lower, the ministry states water flow is maintained, with seasonal decreases expected due to reservoir water accumulation for future needs.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Tighten Regulations for Debt Collectors and Pawnshops Amidst Rising Complaints
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to toughen requirements for debt collection agencies and pawnshops due to a rise in consumer complaints. The financial regulator noted unfair practices by some collectors and an increase in loans from pawnshops as consumers shift from PDL companies. Stricter rules on loan conditions and consumer protection are being prepared for both sectors.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belgium to Expand Cooperation in Rare Earths, Investments, and Visas
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and the King of Belgium, Philippe, have agreed to expand cooperation in critical minerals, energy, industry, agriculture, logistics, and digital technologies. Belgium has invested over $15 billion in Kazakhstan since 2005. Tokayev pledged personal oversight of Belgian company projects in Kazakhstan, and visa procedures for official passport holders have been simplified.

item.title: 12 Village Leaders Punished in East Kazakhstan for Unsanctioned Landfills
item.description: Twelve village leaders in the East Kazakhstan region have been administratively punished for failing to properly control unsanctioned landfills. The prosecutor's office reported the discovery of 15 illegal dumps during an environmental campaign. In total, 177 individuals were fined for violating beautification rules, and the fines have been paid.

item.title: Nobel Prize in Economics Awarded to Two American Scientists for Macroeconomic Models
item.description: American scientists Robert Hall and Michael Woodford will receive the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics for developing macroeconomic models that expanded the possibilities of stabilization economic policy. Their research aids in analyzing economic fluctuations and assessing the effectiveness of measures to maintain economic stability.

item.title: Kabul Faces Water "Day Zero" in 2029 Due to Increased Demand and Climate Change, Expert Warns
item.description: An expert warns that Kabul could face a water "Day Zero" in 2029, a year earlier than previously projected, due to factors including returning migrants, rapid construction, climate change, and water network losses. Urgent action is needed to avert a severe water crisis in the capital.

item.title: Kazakhstan Grain Exports Face Russian Rail Bottleneck to Estonian Ports
item.description: Russian Railways has rejected October requests to transport grain from Kazakhstan to Estonian ports, citing insufficient rail capacity. This blocks the usual route for high-value durum wheat and oilseed flax. Disruptions in the Black Sea have redirected Russian grain, increasing pressure on Russian rail infrastructure and transit routes through Eastern Europe.

item.title: Plague Foci Cover 40% of Kazakhstan; Experts Assess Infection Risk
item.description: Natural plague foci occupy 40% of Kazakhstan, raising concerns despite the disease's historical perception. While a recent suspected plague case in Russia was not confirmed, Kazakh specialists are monitoring territories and assessing risks. Modern medicine can effectively combat plague, but vigilance is necessary to prevent human infection.

item.title: Afghanistan's Political Upheaval Creates Fragile Lives and Economic Insecurity for Citizens
item.description: Afghanistan's frequent government changes have consistently disrupted citizens' lives, impacting livelihoods, investments, and job security. The text highlights how political instability ties economic and legal futures to power structures, leaving many vulnerable to upheaval and uncertain about their prospects.

item.title: Turkmen citizens desire return to normalcy amid international isolation
item.description: Despite a recent CIS summit highlighting Turkmenistan's international engagement, citizens express a desire for openness and normalized relations with neighbors. They are concerned about isolation, strict controls, and economic stagnation. Some intellectuals hope for genuine cooperation with Central Asian states, considering regional and global conflicts.

item.title: Two Tajik migrants hailed heroes for rescuing locals from a fire in Russia
item.description: Two Tajik citizens, Khisravshoh Malik and Zohirshoh Hasanov, are being praised for their bravery in rescuing two local residents from a fire in a Sterlitamak shopping center. The incident occurred in September, and the migrants reportedly entered the burning building through a window to save the individuals before firefighters arrived.

item.title: Kandahar Factories Face Closure Due to Severe Power Shortages, Industrialists Report
item.description: Industrialists in Kandahar report that over two-thirds of the province's factories have closed due to severe electricity shortages. Approximately 280 out of 400 factories have ceased operations in the past two years. Remaining factories are reducing activity by up to 50 percent, facing potential closure if the situation persists.

item.title: Uzbekistan National Judo Team Wins Bronze Medal at World Championships
item.description: The Uzbekistan national judo team secured a bronze medal at the World Championships. The team defeated Germany and Georgia in the qualifying rounds but lost to Russia 3:4 in the semifinals. This achievement highlights the team's competitive performance on the international stage.

item.title: Navoiazot to Establish Intelligent Management Center for Production Monitoring
item.description: Navoiazot Joint Stock Company is establishing an Intelligent Management Center to monitor and analyze production processes using digital technologies. The center will collect and process data on performance, resources, and equipment, utilizing AI and automated tools to identify potential disruptions, optimize resource consumption, and enhance product quality.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Urges Migrants to Return, Citing Job Availability and Housing Projects
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has called on citizens working abroad to return home, stating that job opportunities and housing are available. He highlighted ongoing construction of apartments by the State Mortgage Company to facilitate the return of labor migrants. The president emphasized that work exists in the country and encouraged citizens to invite their relatives working overseas to come back.

item.title: Kazakh President Dissolves Regional Assemblies, Calls for Early Elections
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has dissolved all regional representative assemblies (maslikhats) and ordered early elections. The Central Election Commission is tasked with organizing the snap polls. Tokayev cited changes in the country's party system, including the planned merger of the ruling Amanat party with Adilet, as the reason for the dissolution.

item.title: Tajikistan Develops Three Solar Power Station Projects for Residential Homes
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Energy and Water Resources has developed three standard designs for solar power stations for private homes. These projects offer different installation options based on capacity and site specifics, including rooftop and ground-mounted systems.

item.title: Tajikistan's Mufti Proposes Pre-Marital Courses to Combat Rising Divorce Rates
item.description: Tajikistan's Council of Ulema Chairman, Saidmukarram Abdukodirzoda, has urged couples to attend special courses and read literature on family life before marriage, citing concerns over divorces among young families. He suggested that such preparation, which includes religious, psychological, and social aspects, could reduce divorce rates, citing an unnamed country where divorces dropped from 80-85% to 25% after implementing similar courses.
